do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Users can manage an approved document category for the intended entity type.
steps: Identify the target entity type and whether qualifiers should restrict the type to a subset.
Select the associated file type and review its security and required preferred-file settings.
Create or review the entity document type under `Admin Tools > Settings > Document Types`.
Configure manual selection, maximum documents, qualifiers, and default naming as needed.
For Person, inspect the existing Person Profile document surface.
For another entity, place a Documents block on a page with that entity in context.
Configure the block’s Entity Type, allowed Document Types, and security-button visibility.
Test with a non-sensitive file and an authorized test role.
Verify add, list, download, and security behavior separately. (Configure Entity Documents, Add the Block)
Confirm that the page supplies the intended entity in context.
Confirm that the Documents block’s Entity Type matches that context.
Inspect the block’s selected Document Types.
Inspect the document type’s Entity Type and any qualifier column and value.
Confirm that the document type is manually selectable if a user is trying to add it manually.
Confirm that any maximum-documents limit has not been reached. (Configure Entity Documents, Add the Block)
title: Recipe: Configure an entity document type and management surface

do_not_assume: The first 15 rows represent every record.
General Lava features all work in Word.
GroupMember rows retain GroupMember as the top-level row type.
Template visibility implies authorization to generate it.
goal: A global or personal template generates the intended output from a known grid source.
steps: Choose personal or global scope.
For a global template, configure template security before broad use.
Choose Word or HTML based on the required output.
Open the target grid’s merge action.
inspect the row count, first 15 rows, and available merge fields.
Decide whether output should remain one row per person or combine family members.
Build the template using only the Lava features supported by that format.
For Word, choose whole-document repetition or `{% Next %}` multi-record layout deliberately.
Use straight quotation marks in all Lava expressions.
Run a small representative test and inspect the generated content before using the full population. (Administrate Merge Templates, Use Merge Documents, Create a Merge Document)
Replace curved quotation marks with straight quotation marks.
Check whether the template uses unsupported Word features: `if`, `raw`, or `lava` tags, Lava commands, or shortcodes.
Inspect the available merge fields for the actual grid source.
If the source contains GroupMember rows, use the exposed person row and access membership data through `Row.GroupMember`.
Check whether `{% Next %}` is present and whether the desired output is one complete document per row or multiple rows in one layout. (Create a Merge Document, Using Lava with Merge Documents)
title: Recipe: Create and validate a merge template

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A reviewed signature template can generate and store signed documents using the intended signer experience.
steps: Open `Admin Tools > Settings > Signature Documents`.
Define a clear name, description, and document term.
Select typed or drawn input; prefer typed unless an approved requirement justifies storing drawn-signature PII.
Select the signed-document file type.
Select the completion System Communication.
Decide whether completed documents can remain valid for future use.
Author the Lava body and verify that its attribute keys match the intended workflow or registration inputs.
Add `<!-- [[ SignatureDetails ]] -->` wherever explicit or repeated signature placement is required.
Preview or test with non-sensitive representative data.
Verify the stored document and completion email as separate outcomes. (Set Up Electronic Signatures)
Inspect the fixed **Signature Document Template** action setting.
Inspect the dynamic template ID, GUID, or workflow attribute.
If both are populated, treat the fixed template as authoritative because it takes precedence.
Confirm that the selected template is active; Rock 16.1 fixed inactive-template filtering in workflow actions.
Confirm that attribute values contain the expected ID or GUID representation. (Use Electronic Signatures in a Workflow, Rock Core Release Notes)
title: Recipe: Configure a signature template

do_not_assume: Assigned To and Applies To are interchangeable.
A dynamic template value overrides a fixed template.
A bulk launch contains a ConnectionRequest or another pipeline entity.
Do not populate the fixed field if dynamic selection is intended.
goal: The workflow presents the correct document to the correct signer and retains the resulting signed file.
steps: Decide whether the action uses one fixed template or a dynamic template ID/GUID.
Do not populate the fixed field if dynamic selection is intended.
Map Applies To, Assigned To, and Signed By to explicit Person attributes.
Add a Binary File workflow attribute for the resulting signature document and select the intended signed-document file type.
Define a Lava-enabled document name.
Test logged-in and applicable non-logged-in behavior because login affects Signed By handling.
Verify the template selected, subject, assigned signer, actual signer, stored PDF, and receipt delivery.
If the workflow has multiple launch contexts, condition any unrelated entity mutations on the presence of their required context. (Use Electronic Signatures in a Workflow, RockU Workflows)
Inspect the fixed **Signature Document Template** action setting.
Inspect the dynamic template ID, GUID, or workflow attribute.
If both are populated, treat the fixed template as authoritative because it takes precedence.
Confirm that the selected template is active; Rock 16.1 fixed inactive-template filtering in workflow actions.
Confirm that attribute values contain the expected ID or GUID representation. (Use Electronic Signatures in a Workflow, Rock Core Release Notes)
title: Recipe: Add an electronic signature to a workflow

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Each registrant receives the correct signature requirement through the supported registration flow.
steps: Confirm the external page uses the Obsidian Registration Entry block.
Confirm the signature template uses Rock’s built-in electronic-signature system.
Edit the registration template under `Tools > Event Registration`.
Select the required signature document.
Review whether birthdate should be required so adult/child assignment is reliable.
Test an adult registering themselves.
Test an adult registering a child.
Test a matched person with an existing valid document for the same required template.
Verify the registrant relationship and displayed completion state from the registration instance.
Confirm receipt PDF generation and delivery separately. (Use Electronic Signatures in Event Registrations)
Confirm the external registration page uses the Obsidian Registration Entry block.
Confirm the required template is a current built-in electronic-signature template rather than a legacy-provider document.
Inspect the registration template’s Required Signature Document selection.
Confirm the registrant’s person match, signature-document relationship, required template, and validity.
Determine whether the installation includes the Rock 18.3 registrant relationship fix and migration. (Use Electronic Signatures in Event Registrations, Rock Core Release Notes)
title: Recipe: Configure an event-registration signature requirement

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: An authorized administrator verifies the signed record and resends the existing completion email when appropriate.
steps: Confirm the installed Rock version and applicable security authority.
Navigate to `Admin Tools > Settings > Signature Documents`.
Select the exact signature document template.
Locate the intended document record.
Open its details and inspect the signed file.
Confirm the intended recipient before resending.
Use the documented resend-completion-email action.
Verify communication delivery through the communications system rather than treating the button click as delivery proof. (Manage Signature Documents)
title: Recipe: Review a completed signature document and resend its receipt

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: The organization has a justified local or external rendering path.
steps: Identify whether the host can run Puppeteer or Chrome.
If it cannot, plan an external rendering service.
If it can, evaluate expected signature volume and concurrent server load.
When local rendering poses excessive load, select and review an external service.
Configure the **PDF External Render Endpoint** under System Configuration.
Test preview, completed signing, PDF storage, and receipt delivery.
Load-test only within an approved non-production or otherwise controlled scope.
Document provider, privacy, credential, capacity, and failure-handling ownership. (Generate PDFs for Electronic Signature Documents)
Separate rendering from communication delivery: first determine whether the signed PDF exists.
Inspect the signature template’s file type and completion System Communication.
Inspect the **PDF External Render Endpoint** system setting.
Determine whether the host can run Puppeteer or Chrome.
If local rendering is supported, review whether concurrent volume is exhausting server capacity.
If external rendering is required, verify endpoint configuration and reachability without exposing credentials.
After PDF generation succeeds, troubleshoot the completion email through the communications system. (Generate PDFs for Electronic Signature Documents, Set Up Electronic Signatures)
title: Recipe: Decide whether to offload signed-PDF rendering

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A maintainer determines whether a community recipe is safe and still necessary without executing destructive steps by default.
steps: First test the official completed-document resend action to determine whether it satisfies the need.
Define whether the desired outcome is receipt redelivery, a new signature request, clearing a group requirement, or replacing an invalid registrant signature.
Review the installed Rock version and relevant fixes.
Read the community recipe as a design example, not as approved core behavior.
Identify every delete, relationship reset, command SQL, security-disabled entity access, and bulk-action path.
Confirm backups, rollback, authorization, schema compatibility, record scope, and a non-production test plan.
Prefer supported workflow actions and current core behavior where they meet the requirement.

Stop before executing SQL, deleting signature documents, clearing registrant relationships, or deleting workflows unless those exact mutations are separately reviewed and authorized. (Re-Send Signature Documents from Registrant, Resend a Group Requirement Helper Workflow)
title: Recipe: Evaluate a community resend or reset workaround
